excerpt: ScrapeOps Proxy Tester benchmarks 20+ proxy providers against the exact site you want to scrape and emails a ranked report on success rate, speed and cost. Free.
content:
Proxy Tester is a free tool from ScrapeOps, a web-scraping tools company, for choosing a proxy provider. Instead of relying on generic rankings, you enter the page you actually want to scrape and how often and how much you plan to scrape it. The tester sends requests through more than 20 residential, datacenter, mobile, proxy-API and unblocker services, checks that each "successful" response is a real page and not a ban or CAPTCHA page, and emails you a ranked report, usually in about 5 to 20 minutes.

The report covers success rate, average latency of successful requests, bandwidth or API credits used, the cheapest plan from each provider that fits your volume, and an estimated cost per million pages. The makers say the value ranking groups providers into performance tiers first and then ranks them mainly by cost within each tier.

The makers on Product Hunt are Ian Kerins, who describes himself as bootstrapping ScrapeOps, and Joe Kearney. Proxy Tester launched there on 9 August 2026, hunted by Hiten Shah, and finished #4 for the day with 210 upvotes and 12 comments (as of 14 October 2026). ScrapeOps also sells its own proxy aggregator, which appears in the benchmark alongside other providers.

We have not tested Proxy Tester ourselves. This page brings together the tool's own page, ScrapeOps' site and its Product Hunt launch, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.summary_short: Benchmarks 20+ proxy providers against the exact site you want to scrape

gallery.alt: ScrapeOps Proxy Tester overview: enter a target URL, run benchmarks, compare results in a success-rate chart, choose the best provider
Proxy Tester configuration step asking how often and how many pages a month you scrape, with optional extra domains
Sample Proxy Tester report with a success-rate comparison chart and a table of providers' success rate, latency, credits and price

paragraphs: Ian Kerins says that after talking with hundreds of developers building scraping pipelines, the same question kept coming up: which proxy provider should I use for this website? There is no universal answer, because a provider that works well on one site can do badly on another.
Most teams end up buying credits, running manual tests and comparing logs for days. Proxy Tester is meant to replace that: you submit your target URL and benchmark many providers at once.
launch_story.attribution: Ian Kerins, maker, on Product Hunt

use_cases: Choosing a proxy provider for a hard-to-scrape site behind anti-bot protection
Checking whether a cheaper provider performs as well on your target
Estimating the monthly cost of scraping a site at your volume

fit: run scraping pipelines and pay for proxies
scrape sites protected by anti-bot systems such as Cloudflare
want a comparison based on your own target, not vendor claims
not_fit: don't want to give an email address: reports are sent by email, which one commenter disliked
need a fully independent benchmark: ScrapeOps' own aggregator is one of the providers tested

pricing.intro: The tool's own FAQ says the Proxy Tester is free. No credit card is needed.

plans.name: Proxy Tester
plans.detail: Benchmark 20+ providers against your target URL; ranked report by email in about 5 to 20 minutes

notes: ScrapeOps sells other products, such as its proxy aggregator, separately; its site offers 1,000 free requests to try it.

alternatives.intro: The usual alternative is testing providers by hand with trial credits. Some publishers also run general proxy benchmarks.

items.name: Manual testing with provider trials
items.what: Buying or using trial credits from several providers and comparing logs yourself
items.difference: Exact for your setup but slow; the makers say it often takes teams days.

alternatives.more: Proxy Tester's sample report compares providers such as Zyte API, Scrape.do, ScraperAPI, Scrapfly and Bright Data alongside ScrapeOps.

liked: Benchmarking against the real target URL instead of generic rankings
Grouping providers by performance tier before ranking by cost
asked: How fresh results are (each report is a live snapshot for your URL at that moment)
Whether the value score can be weighted differently (currently weighted toward cost; one commenter asked for adjustable weighting)
criticised: One commenter objected to having to give an email address to get the report

quotes.text: target-specific benchmarking over generic rankings makes way more sense, proxy performance is so site-dependent.
quotes.author: Sabber Ahamed

quotes.text: I've watched a provider ace one retail site and get stonewalled by another with the same config
quotes.author: Akbar B

pros: Tests on your actual target and validates that responses aren't ban pages
Estimates cost per million pages at your volume
cons: ScrapeOps' own aggregator is among the providers ranked
Results are a snapshot and can change when a site updates its defences

quotes.author: Sabber Ahamed
quotes.text: is the value score weighted evenly across success/latency/cost or can you tune it per use case?
quotes.reply: Ian Kerins said it is weighted more toward cost: providers are grouped into performance tiers by success rate and latency, then ranked mainly by cost within a tier.

x.none: Apart from ScrapeOps' own account, we found no posts on X clearly about Proxy Tester.
